title: Does huge volume at a new high mean the top is in? I checked 438 cases in Indian stocks.
author: iktisab
selftext:
Common rule: huge volume at the highs = sell.



I checked 438 cases in 24 big Indian stocks (2010–2026). 20 trading days later:

\- 45% were lower

\- Normal new highs without the spike: 46% lower



So the spike alone tells you almost nothing.



What helped more: if price stayed above the spike day's low for the next 3 days, only 41% ended lower. If it broke that low, 51% did.



Limits: only today's big stocks, daily data, no costs. Not advice. Happy to hear criticism.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the 41 vs 51 split uses the 3 days after the spike, so if the 20-day clock starts on the spike day, part of the outcome is already inside the filter. a stock that broke the spike low has already dropped by day 3. start the 20 days on day 4 and see if the gap holds.

replies.author: iktisab
replies.body: I have tested it all and this was the end result.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: fair, if the 20 days already start after the spike window then the filter is clean. what I'd check next is how many of the hits came from the same few weeks, one rough month can carry a split like that. a ten year replay with no peeking ahead is what Quantradin does on US stocks.
